subject: Materials Science
title: Responsible Nanotechnology
description: A quick win: understand Responsible Nanotechnology.

hook.text: A technology with the power to transform medicine and energy also demands new rules — responsible nanotechnology.

buildup.text: Safe-by-design builds safety into nanomaterials from the start — choosing less toxic cores and biodegradable coatings.

discovery.text: Green nanosynthesis uses plant extracts instead of harsh chemicals — reducing waste and energy use.

twist.text: Public perception lags behind science — surveys show people fear nanomaterials they use daily in sunscreen and food.

climax.text: Standards bodies now define nano-specific testing, labeling, and disposal — governance catching up to innovation.

punchline.text: The smallest materials demand the biggest responsibility — trust is key.

quiz.question: What does safe-by-design mean in nanotechnology?
options: Making nanoparticles larger to avoid nano-specific risks
Incorporating safety features like low-toxicity cores and biodegradable coatings from the start
Only using nanomaterials in controlled laboratory environments
